record.title: Characterisation of mechanical properties of materials used in 3D printing
claim_notes: Attribution: Aniskevich Andrey and Bulderberga Olga (2023), Characterisation of mechanical properties of materials used in 3D printing, Zenodo dataset, version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8089569; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8089568. Creator order and spelling follow the Zenodo version record.

Annex 3.1. Characterisation of mechanical properties.xlsx: 1391320 bytes; published MD5 c4842898d2c389ccd7a902691d8a4fa3; independently computed SHA-256 830b2c9277dcc2d03265b63e311a5e7089c258ebb6a389b45d07601ae4b2e4e7.

Only sparse reference-filament measurements and identification cells are curated. Numeric XML lexical values are preserved without changing or recalculating them; source text is organized and summarized into catalog fields. The raw workbook, images, full worksheets and extensive prose are excluded.
The selected measured cells are Tensile modulus E:H: reference filament 2.8 mm, testing at 10 mm/min, MPa. The ISO 527-2-labelled C column is separate and does not establish the measured E:H method.

Samples C27 states that three to five specimens were tested per series and average data were used. Exact row-specific n is unstated. The avedev columns are retained as source-labelled deviations without assuming SD, SE, confidence intervals or a defined calculation.

Zenodo version metadata.license.id and DataCite concept rightsList independently report CC BY 4.0; DataCite HasVersion identifies 10.5281/zenodo.8089569. Attribution, source/version links and license link are retained. Catalog organization and original qualification notes are adaptations; no source endorsement or relicensing under the project MIT license is asserted. Manufacturer evidence has its own rights scope.

provenance.method: Official Zenodo version metadata and DataCite concept metadata checked; one bounded workbook download independently matched the published size and MD5. Original worksheet cells and XML numeric storage were inspected without formula execution, raw-data reanalysis, new experiments or independent scientific approval.

record.title: Tough PLA Safety Data Sheet
claim_notes: SDS ID UM00009, version 2.0, revised 2022-12-22 and superseding 2019-01-14. The year/date identify the document revision, not its original publication or the study's experiment date.

PDF page 1, section 1.1, identifies Tough PLA as a mixture and explicitly covers Black and White among the listed colors. PDF page 2, section 3.2, names Polylactic acid and Acrylic polymer in the mixture comments.

Only the brief constituent/product-family classification fact supports mat_aniskevich_2023_ultimaker_tough_pla. Black and White remain separate measured workbook states under that qualified identity; their color, source code or differing measurements alone do not create extra identities.

The dated source supplies product-family context before the 2023 dataset deposit; no specimen manufacture date, experimental date, exact lot recipe or identical complete pigment/additive recipe across colors is established.

Neither workbook code 20231 nor 202300 appears in this SDS. Both remain uncorrected workbook literals, not independently authenticated manufacturer SKUs. No PMMA identity, constituent fraction, ingredient function, numerical manufacturer property, purity or complete formulation is imported.
Inspected PDF: 496191 bytes; SHA-256 3b97d600b92f44da56a4c5c8bae029dddbc4b2d400d3c7501cafed9b7aaf69cf. Raw PDF, rendered pages and full extracted text remain external evidence only.

No explicit open reuse license was verified for this manufacturer SDS. Only sparse attributed identity/classification facts and original qualification notes are proposed. The separate Zenodo dataset CC BY 4.0 license is not inherited by this source; no blanket asset reuse, MIT relicensing or legal-clearance claim is made.

provenance.method: One bounded direct acquisition from the official Ultimaker support-files origin; exact bytes hashed, all-page text inspected for source identifiers, and selected PDF pages 1 and 2 rendered and visually cross-checked. This is source-transcription/identity context only, not a tested-lot composition assay or independent scientific validation.

product_form.notes: Source-reported nominal form; no independent diameter measurement or substitution of later product diameters.

processing.notes: Reference-filament manufacturing history is not stated. Nozzle/bed temperatures and layer thickness in Tested materials!E:G describe printing and are not imported here.

temper_or_heat_treatment.notes: No reference-filament heat-treatment or annealing history is stated.

conditioning.notes: Pre-test drying, storage time, temperature and humidity for this filament series are not stated.

reinforcement.notes: The workbook does not report a quantitative filler assay. Separate manufacturer identity evidence is restricted to classification; no filler fraction, morphology or exact-lot certification is inferred.

porosity.notes: No physical porosity or void fraction is reported for the reference filament; no zero porosity is inferred.

orientation.notes: A source-specific orientation convention, gauge geometry and anisotropy characterization are not stated for the reference-filament measurements.

filament.basis_note: Tensile modulus!E:H reports measured reference-filament tensile results at the source-stated rate. Samples!C27 says three to five specimens were tested per series and average data were used. The source-reported average is retained without assigning exact row-specific n, pooling weights or a statistical definition of avedev.

temperature.notes: Numerical tensile-test temperature is not stated. Printing nozzle/bed temperatures are not test temperatures.

test_standard.notes: The ISO 527-2 label belongs to the separate reference column C; it does not establish the method for measured columns E:H.

test_method.text: Tensile testing of reference filament 2.8 mm; source reports E-mod and tensile strength
test_method.notes: Instrument, extensometry, gauge length, grip separation and modulus extraction window are not stated; no yield/ultimate qualifier or isotropic Young's-modulus interpretation is added.

direction.notes: No additional source-specific tensile direction convention is stated for the reference filament.

method_definition.definition: Source-reported series-average tensile reference-filament measurements in Tensile modulus!E:H. E-mod is retained as tensile_modulus. The separate ISO-labelled reference column C, extruded fibers and printed dogbones are excluded; no recalculation from raw specimens is performed.

claim_notes: SDS ID UM00009, version 2.0, revised 2022-12-22 and superseding 2019-01-14. The year/date identify the document revision, not its original publication or the study's experiment date.

PDF page 1, section 1.1, identifies Tough PLA as a mixture and explicitly covers Black and White among the listed colors. PDF page 2, section 3.2, names Polylactic acid and Acrylic polymer in the mixture comments.

Only the brief constituent/product-family classification fact supports mat_aniskevich_2023_ultimaker_tough_pla. Black and White remain separate measured workbook states under that qualified identity; their color, source code or differing measurements alone do not create extra identities.

The dated source supplies product-family context before the 2023 dataset deposit; no specimen manufacture date, experimental date, exact lot recipe or identical complete pigment/additive recipe across colors is established.

Neither workbook code 20231 nor 202300 appears in this SDS. Both remain uncorrected workbook literals, not independently authenticated manufacturer SKUs. No PMMA identity, constituent fraction, ingredient function, numerical manufacturer property, purity or complete formulation is imported.

tough_pla.identity_scope_proposal: One source-qualified Ultimaker Tough PLA formulation family represented by the Black and White reference-filament series in Aniskevich and Bulderberga (2023). The 22 December 2022 manufacturer SDS names polylactic acid and an unspecified acrylic polymer and covers both colors. This constituent evidence supports a curated formulation distinction from the generic PLA representative; no absence of acrylic additives in other PLA products is asserted. Supplier, product name, color, numeric code and differing measured values alone do not establish identity. The document supports product-family applicability and does not authenticate workbook codes 20231 or 202300, the tested lots, or identical complete color recipes. Acrylic-polymer chemistry, constituent proportions/functions, pigment/additive recipe and chemical purity remain unknown. No PMMA or constituent fraction is inferred.
tough_pla.basis: The official SDS revision dated 2022-12-22 names Tough PLA, Black and White, and PLA plus an acrylic polymer. The dated document precedes the 2023 dataset deposit and bridges the workbook supplier/product names to the manufacturer formulation family. No experiment or manufacture date is established, so temporal applicability is expressly family-level.

identity_evidence.locator: PDF p.1 section 1.1, Tough PLA trade name and Black/White color coverage; PDF p.2 section 3.2, mixture comments

tough_pla.two_state_rationale: The independent original-XML readback confirms two distinct measured color series and exact workbook joins. Both names fall within the dated manufacturer product/color coverage. Including both states preserves source groups rather than certifying either numeric code as a SKU. Black-only selection has no superior SKU verification; the SDS authenticates neither code. Do not average or pool the rows.
